take: Kingfisher Golf comes out of Dallas by way of PepsiCo’s creative department. Founder Fiona Cohen spent years as an art director specializing in animation and motion design before launching a golf label that treats apparel like a design project — not a merchandise run. The tees are screen-printed at Lewellyn’s Print Shop in Old East Dallas. The polos are produced by the same factory teams behind the big-brand performance shirts you already own. Everything stays under $56.
story_extra: The brand’s breakout moment was the “Worst Golfer in Dallas” contest — a city-wide search for the most entertainingly bad golfer, covered by D Magazine and backed by a cream heavyweight tee that became the brand’s fastest seller. The winner, Colin Perry, is now Kingfisher’s first sponsored athlete. It’s the kind of move that only works when a brand genuinely doesn’t take itself too seriously. Heading into the second half of summer, the lineup has grown into a legitimate collection: patterned performance polos, boxy streetwear-cut tees, and a deep hat wall that covers every style from camo trucker to unstructured dad cap. Nothing flashy, nothing over-engineered — just Dallas golf energy with a design eye behind it.

Revisited, August 2026: Kingfisher had a moment this spring — D Magazine covered the "Worst Golfer in Dallas" contest, which ended with Colin Perry crowned as the brand's first sponsored athlete (prize: lessons and general glory). Since our first post, the whole catalog was repriced — polos now $65, tees $40, caps $36 — and the range roughly doubled: the Kit, Mechanic, Navy Zipper, and Cream polos below are new, along with the Golfmobile and Athletics tees and a DAL cap wall that now runs eight colorways deep. Prices updated throughout.
